content.comment_body: Hello! I am working on a network project with three [product_name] devices. Over time, there have been many changes made directly to the device parameters, so my project on the computer is now outdated. What is the simplest way to update my project to match the device’s current configuration? Thanks in advance.

You can transfer any program from the respective [product_name] device to your PC. However, depending on the program size, the transferred version can appear disorganized and lose texts such as comments or input/output names. To handle this, you may compare the downloaded program with your original project using [product_name] comparison tools, which display differences and let you update your original project accordingly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users managing [product_name] network projects encounter difficulties in maintaining synchronization between device-side modifications and their computer project files. Updating the local project to include changes made directly on devices is not straightforward and often leads to loss of valuable metadata such as comments and I/O labels. Comparison tools can help identify differences, but the process remains inconvenient and can negatively impact project clarity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking a straightforward and dependable way to synchronize the computer project with direct changes made on [product_name] devices, while preserving important metadata and maintaining project readability.
